description: Pineapple Buns, or Bo Lo Bao, are a beloved Hong Kong bakery classic featuring a fluffy, slightly sweet bread base crowned with a crisp, crumbly, and sweet topping that resembles a pineapple's skin. Despite their name, these golden buns contain no pineapple, offering a delightful contrast of textures and flavors in every bite. They are perfect enjoyed warm with a slice of butter or as a comforting snack with milk tea.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine 250g all-purpose flour, 30g granulated sugar, 4g instant dry yeast, and 3g salt. Add the large egg and 100ml warm milk, mixing until a shaggy dough forms. Knead on a lightly floured surface for 10-15 minutes until smooth and elastic. Incorporate 30g softened unsalted butter and knead for another 5 minutes until fully absorbed and the dough passes the windowpane test.

instructions.title: First Proofing
instructions.text: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 60-90 minutes, or until doubled in size.

instructions.title: Prepare the Pineapple Topping
instructions.text: While the dough proofs, cream 60g softened unsalted butter and 60g granulated sugar together until light and fluffy. Beat in the egg yolk and 1 tbsp evaporated milk until well combined. Gradually add 120g all-purpose flour, 10g powdered milk, and 2g baking powder, mixing until a soft dough forms. Do not overmix. Cover and chill in the refrigerator for 30 minutes.

instructions.title: Shape the Buns
instructions.text: Once the dough has doubled, gently punch it down and divide into 8 equal portions. Roll each portion into a smooth ball. On a lightly floured surface, divide the chilled topping dough into 8 equal portions. Flatten each topping portion into a disc large enough to cover the top of a bun. Carefully place a topping disc over each dough ball, gently pressing to adhere and shaping it to cover about two-thirds of the bun's surface.

instructions.title: Second Proofing and Scoring
instructions.text: Arrange the shaped buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let them rise in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until visibly puffed. Preheat your oven to 180°C (350°F). Just before baking, gently brush the topping with an egg wash made from 1 egg yolk and 1 tsp water, and use a knife to score a crisscross pattern on the topping, mimicking a pineapple.

instructions.title: Bake the Buns
instructions.text: Bake the Pineapple Buns in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the buns are cooked through. If the topping browns too quickly, you can tent them loosely with foil.

instructions.title: Cool and Serve
instructions.text: Remove the buns from the oven and transfer them to a wire rack to cool slightly. Pineapple Buns are best enjoyed warm, often with a slice of cold butter inserted into a freshly split bun.

tips: Ensure your dough passes the 'windowpane test' for optimal texture: a small piece of dough should stretch thinly enough to see light through it without tearing.
For a more intense pineapple flavor in the topping, you can add a tiny pinch of pineapple extract, though traditionally Bo Lo Bao contains no actual pineapple.
Store leftover Pineapple Buns at room temperature in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Reheat briefly in a toaster oven for best results.
article:
The aroma of freshly baked goods often holds a special place in our hearts, evoking feelings of comfort and nostalgia. Among the myriad of delights from Chinese bakeries, few capture the imagination quite like the Pineapple Bun, or Bo Lo Bao (菠蘿包). With its iconic crackled, golden crust reminiscent of a pineapple and a pillowy soft interior, this beloved pastry is a staple in Hong Kong-style cafes and dim sum restaurants worldwide. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that magic at home, you're in luck – we're diving deep into the ultimate Pineapple Bun Recipe, offering a comprehensive guide to mastering this Chinese baking classic.

## What is Pineapple Bun (Bo Lo Bao)?

Despite its name, the Pineapple Bun contains no actual pineapple. The "pineapple" moniker comes purely from its distinctive topping – a sweet, crumbly, and slightly crunchy crust that bakes into a beautiful golden pattern, resembling the skin of a pineapple. Beneath this glorious cap lies a wonderfully soft, fluffy, and slightly sweet bread, making for a delightful contrast of textures and flavors.

Originating in Hong Kong, Bo Lo Bao quickly became a culinary icon, synonymous with cha chaan teng (Hong Kong-style diners) and traditional dim sum houses. It's cherished as a breakfast item, an afternoon snack, or simply a comforting treat enjoyed with a cup of milk tea. Its universal appeal lies in its simplicity and the sheer satisfaction it delivers with every bite. The bread itself is often enriched with milk and eggs, contributing to its tender crumb, while the topping, made from flour, sugar, butter, and egg, provides that essential sweetness and crispness.

## Ingredients for Homemade Pineapple Buns

Crafting the perfect Bo Lo Bao requires attention to both the bread dough and its signature topping. Here’s what you’ll need for your homemade Pineapple Bun Recipe:

For the Bread Dough:
*   Bread Flour: High protein content for a chewy, airy texture.
*   Granulated Sugar: Adds sweetness and aids in yeast activation.
*   Salt: Balances flavors.
*   Active Dry Yeast: The leavening agent.
*   Milk (warm): Activates yeast and adds richness.
*   Large Egg: For color, richness, and structure.
*   Unsalted Butter (softened): Enhances flavor and tenderness.

For the Crumb Topping:
*   All-Purpose Flour: The base for the crumb.
*   Granulated Sugar: For sweetness and crispness.
*   Unsalted Butter (cold, cubed): Crucial for a crumbly texture.
*   Egg Yolk: Binds the topping and adds richness and color.
*   Evaporated Milk or Regular Milk: Just a touch, if needed, to bring the topping together.
*   Baking Powder (optional): Some recipes add a pinch for extra crispness.

For the Egg Wash:
*   One Egg (beaten): For a golden-brown finish on the topping.

## Step-by-Step Guide to Making Bo Lo Bao

This comprehensive Pineapple Bun Recipe will guide you through each stage, ensuring a successful bake.

1.  Prepare the Bread Dough:
    *   Activate Yeast: In a large bowl, combine warm milk, a pinch of sugar, and active dry yeast. Let it sit for 5-10 minutes until frothy.
    *   Mix Dry Ingredients: In another bowl, whisk together bread flour, remaining sugar, and salt.
    *   Combine: Add the egg to the yeast mixture, then pour into the dry ingredients. Mix until a shaggy dough forms.
    *   Knead: Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured surface or use a stand mixer with a dough hook. Knead for 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth and elastic.
    *   Add Butter: Gradually incorporate the softened butter, kneading until fully absorbed and the dough is soft, smooth, and passes the windowpane test (can be stretched thin without tearing).
    *   First Proofing: Place the dough in a lightly oiled bowl, cover with plastic wrap, and let it rise in a warm place for 1-1.5 hours, or until doubled in size.

2.  Make the Crumb Topping:
    *   Cream Butter and Sugar: In a medium bowl, cream together the cold butter and sugar until light and fluffy.
    *   Add Egg Yolk: Beat in the egg yolk until well combined.
    *   Incorporate Flour: Gradually add the all-purpose flour (and baking powder, if using) until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs. If too dry, add a tiny bit of milk or evaporated milk, just enough for it to come together when pressed.
    *   Chill: Form the topping into a disk, wrap in plastic, and chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 minutes. This makes it easier to handle.

3.  Assemble the Buns:
    *   Divide Dough: Once the bread dough has doubled, gently punch it down and divide it into 10-12 equal pieces (around 50-60g each). Roll each piece into a smooth ball.
    *   Prepare Topping: Remove the chilled topping from the fridge. Divide it into the same number of pieces as your dough balls. Flatten each piece of topping into a thin disc, large enough to cover about 2/3 of the bread bun.
    *   Apply Topping: Gently place a topping disc over each bread dough ball, pressing lightly to adhere and smooth it around the top and sides.
    *   Score: Using a butter knife or a dough scraper, gently score a crosshatch pattern onto the topping of each bun. This creates the "pineapple" effect.

4.  Second Proofing:
    *   Arrange Buns: Place the assembled buns on a baking sheet lined with parchment paper, leaving space between them.
    *   Proof Again: Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let them rise in a warm place for another 30-45 minutes, or until noticeably puffy.

5.  Bake the Pineapple Buns:
    *   Preheat Oven: Preheat your oven to 350°F (175°C).
    *   Egg Wash: Gently brush the tops of the buns (specifically the topping) with the beaten egg wash.
    *   Bake: Bake for 15-20 minutes, or until the topping is golden brown and the bread is cooked through.
    *   Cool: Transfer the baked buns to a wire rack to cool slightly before serving.

## Tips for Perfect Pineapple Buns

Even with a detailed Pineapple Bun Recipe, a few expert tips can make all the difference:

*   Don't Over-Knead the Topping: The topping should be crumbly, not smooth and elastic like dough. Overworking it will make it tough.
*   Chill the Topping Thoroughly: A cold topping is easier to handle and less likely to melt too quickly in the oven, helping it retain its shape and pattern.
*   Proper Proofing: Ensure your dough doubles in size during the first proof and becomes puffy during the second. An under-proofed bun will be dense, while an over-proofed one might collapse.
*   Scoring Technique: Use a gentle but firm hand to score the topping. Don't cut too deep into the bread dough, just enough to create the pattern on the crust.
*   Oven Temperature: Keep an eye on your oven. If the topping browns too quickly, you might need to lower the temperature slightly or tent the buns with foil.
*   Use a Scale: For consistent results, especially when dividing dough and topping, a kitchen scale is invaluable.

## Serving Suggestions & Pairings

The classic way to enjoy a Pineapple Bun is fresh out of the oven, often split horizontally and filled with a thick slice of cold butter (known as Bo Lo Yau). The contrast of the warm, sweet bun and the melting, savory butter is simply divine.

Beyond the classic, Bo Lo Bao pairs wonderfully with:
*   Hong Kong-style Milk Tea: The rich, creamy tea is the perfect counterpoint to the bun's sweetness.
*   Coffee or Hot Lemon Tea: Other popular cha chaan teng beverages.
*   Breakfast or Brunch: A satisfying start to the day.
*   Afternoon Tea: A delightful snack to ward off mid-day hunger.

## Variations & Frequently Asked Questions

This Pineapple Bun Recipe is versatile, allowing for delicious adaptations.

Variations:
*   With Fillings: While traditionally plain, many bakeries offer Bo Lo Bao with various fillings. Popular options include sweet custard, red bean paste, or even savory BBQ pork (Char Siu Bo Lo Bao) for a delightful sweet and savory experience.
*   Different Shapes: Though typically round, you can experiment with oval or square shapes.

Frequently Asked Questions:
*   Why is it called Pineapple Bun if there's no pineapple? As mentioned, it's all about the appearance of the crust, which resembles the rough, segmented skin of a pineapple.
*   Can I make the dough ahead of time? Yes, you can prepare the bread dough, let it complete its first proof, then punch it down and refrigerate overnight. Bring it back to room temperature before shaping and adding the topping.
*   How do I store leftover Pineapple Buns? Store them in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 2-3 days. Reheat them briefly in a toaster oven or microwave for the best texture.
*   Is making Bo Lo Bao difficult? While it has several steps, no individual step is overly complex. With a good Pineapple Bun Recipe like this one and a bit of practice, even beginners can achieve fantastic results.
*   What's the key to a crispy topping? Ensuring your butter is cold when making the topping and not overworking it. Chilling the formed topping before baking also helps.

Embracing the art of Chinese baking with this detailed Pineapple Bun Recipe is a truly rewarding experience. The satisfaction of pulling a tray of golden, fragrant Bo Lo Bao from your oven is unparalleled. Whether you enjoy them plain, with butter, or experiment with fillings, these iconic buns are sure to bring a taste of Hong Kong right into your home. So, gather your ingredients, follow these steps, and prepare to delight in the magic of homemade Pineapple Buns!
